paper_metadata.title: Phenotyping juvenile myoclonic epilepsy. Praxis induction as a biomarker of unfavorable prognosis

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the recruitment source (tertiary center) and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, the final sample (45/133) is highly selected based on specific reflex traits, and the use of a tertiary center population may introduce selection bias as these patients often have more refractory epilepsy than the general JME population.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (Praxis Induction) was rigorously defined and measured using both a validated questionnaire and a standardized video-EEG neuropsychological protocol, ensuring high reliability and low risk of misclassification.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: PI... is defined as precipitation of seizures or epileptiform discharges (ED) by complex, cognition-guided tasks, often involving visuomotor coordination and decision making
items.reasoning: The study provides a clear conceptual and operational definition of Praxis Induction.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: PI was ascertained if at least one NPP task produced myoclonic seizures or ED activation (defined as ED per minute during NPP task at least the double of that in baseline EEG)
items.reasoning: The use of video-EEG with a specific neuropsychological protocol and quantitative criteria for ED activation is a highly reliable method.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: defined as ED per minute during NPP task at least the double of that in baseline EEG
items.reasoning: The study uses a pre-defined threshold for ED activation based on established literature (Matsuoka et al.).

items.evidence_snippet: all 133 consecutive patients had a 4–6 h video-EEG monitoring... The sequence of tasks was administered randomly in different patients.
items.reasoning: The protocol was standardized across the entire cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes were measured using seizure calendars, which are standard but rely on patient self-reporting (recall bias). While the definitions of seizure types are clear, the lack of blinding between the PF status and outcome assessment could introduce bias.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Myoclonia and absences were quantified as seizure days per month... GTCS frequency currently was the sum of all seizures occurred over the last year of followup.
items.reasoning: The study clearly defines how seizure frequency and 'seizure freedom' were calculated.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Standard seizure calendars monitored seizure frequency.
items.reasoning: Seizure calendars are standard in clinical practice but are subjective and prone to under-reporting. There is no mention of blinding the outcome assessors to the PI status.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement

items.evidence_snippet: Standard seizure calendars monitored seizure frequency... Patients were followed-up for one to 15 years
items.reasoning: The same monitoring method (calendars) and clinical follow-up setting were used for both groups.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study compares two groups that are well-matched on baseline demographics and epilepsy duration. However, the analysis relies primarily on univariate comparisons. While a multivariate logistic regression is mentioned, the small sample size (n=45) limits the ability to adjust for multiple confounders simultaneously.
